The next chapter of our future as an aerospace company is here, and we are excited about what this means for our employees and customers! Get onboard the Collins Aerospace Operations team and play a part in managing our innovative products from inception to delivery. The Operations team continues to grow and aims to strengthen the connection of Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain and Environment, Health & Safety (EH&S) across Collins Aerospace. In this dynamic environment, you will have the opportunity to network across our businesses and functions, all while improving the productivity, quality and efficiency of our operations worldwide.

Collins Aerospace, a RTX company, is a leader in technologically advanced and intelligent solutions for the global aerospace and defense industry. Collins Aerospace has the capabilities, comprehensive portfolio and expertise to solve customers’ toughest challenges and to meet the demands of a rapidly evolving global market.

About Pulley

Pulley helps the country’s top architects, builders, and retailers speed up every project in their portfolio. With AI-powered permitting intelligence and expert guidance, we eliminate costly delays and bring predictability across the full lifecycle of commercial projects.

Today, permitting is the slowest, most uncertain part of building, spread across 19,000+ jurisdictions with different rules, timelines, and surprises. Pulley gives project teams the clarity and predictability they need to move from planning to opening without delays.

We support rollout programs for brands like J.Crew, Solidcore, and Hibbett Sports, as well as major data center buildouts, EV charging networks, and other commercial projects. Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.

Role Description

The Electrode Engineering teams within the Core Technology group at Form Energy are multidisciplinary and focused on delivering qualified battery anode and cathode designs that meet operational performance targets, at cost and with high reliability, from controlled processes on high-volume manufacturing lines for Form Energy's utility-scale multi-day energy storage system.

Electrode Engineering is hiring a Senior Program Manager, to lead program management efforts for the development of our Iron-Air battery products. As part of our Core Technology Team, you will contribute to bringing our anode and cathode designs into production, through supporting the activities of our mechanical engineering, materials engineering, and battery engineering teams. As a coordinator and communicator, you will drive tracking and reporting of top risks. You will also take tactical ownership of our product design and execution schedule, through prototyping and engineering validation phases – tracking milestones from design release through supplier fabrication and landing at our factory. This will involve close communication with our factory production and operations teams, supply chain, and various design engineers, as well as coordination with other program managers across the company.

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission! If this sounds like the perfect opportunity for you, apply now!

What You'll Do

Drive electrode programs from the prototyping phase into mass production, while managing and communicating schedules across multiple teams to ensure efficient alignment, coordination, and execution
Maintain design release schedules from design reviews through to landing materials, for externally sourced components
Coordinate with supply chain partners on procurement of tools, critical active materials, and components
Organize and provide routine updates on top technical and program risks and issues, communicating key programmatic information inward to the Electrode Engineering organization, and outward to the broader engineering organization.
Improve our program management systems and structures based on best-practices and your personal experience, to effectively integrate with and support Form Energy’s world-class technical team
Proactively identify and frame key decisions and risks, and work with stakeholders to develop decision-quality options; facilitate progress by ensuring appropriate scheduling, resourcing, and prioritization of engineering workflows

What You'll Bring

5+ years of experience in an engineering or technical Program Management role
Bachelor’s degree in a technical field, such as mechanical, materials, chemical, or electrical engineering
Demonstrated experience in hardware R&D programs
Demonstrated experience with contract manufacturers and/or suppliers of high-volume custom components
Excellent communication and organizational skills, ability to communicate & present at all levels
Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously
A growth mindset and bias for action: you treat ambiguity and roadblocks as opportunities to drive progress, not reasons to wait for direction, and you bring real urgency to creating impact

Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.

When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.

To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.

Job Title:
Senior Technical Program Manager

Job Type:
Full-time

Summary

QuEra is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead program management activities around product and service delivery of QuEra’s quantum computers, starting with Aquila and Gemini, and extending to future generations of QuEra systems.

This role is execution-oriented and inherently cross-functional, coordinating work across hardware and software engineering, research and operations. The role includes limited product management responsibilities, scoped to requirements collection and feedback, and is expected to work collaboratively with future dedicated product management hires.

This role is designed to fulfill these goals, and to evolve as the company grows and the needs change:

Ensure reliable delivery and operation of gate-based quantum computers,
Establish a structured feedback loop from customers and users back into engineering, and align customer projects for success,
Support the product development work on QuEra’s systems towards industrial-grade, TRL=9 platforms, through disciplined program execution,
Enable progress tracking and transparent communication across all stakeholders.

Year 1 focus

The main focus in year 1 will be to support the success of QuEra’s overall AIST program which consists of 4 threads centered around our first gate-based system Gemini:

[Product] Launching two product lines on top of the on-prem Gemini machine at AIST: Gemini-QEC, a platform for error correction researchers, and Gemini-NISQ, a platform for NISQ-era application developers. Initial product launches will be followed by planned upgrades and feature releases in quick succession.
[Customers & Projects] Enabling the success of concrete customers and customer projects on the Gemini machine at AIST, which divide into preview projects (leading up to each product/feature release and leveraging close collaboration with the machine team), and GA projects (following each product/feature release and utilizing the generally available capabilities). Customer success in this context will depend on a fine balance of customer experience, data quality, and timely execution of project phases.
[Integration] Completing system integration with access/distribution partners, in two modalities: HPC integration, and cloud integration.
[Development] Achieving milestones in the NEDO program focused on developing the hardware and software systems towards industrial-grade quantum computers by 2030. This development work is not independent of, but rather on the critical path for 1-3.

Key responsibilities

Product:
Translate high-level product goals and technical roadmap into executable plans, milestones, and dependencies.
Track risks, schedules, and cross-team deliverables to ensure on-time, high-quality product launches.
Customers and Projects
Act as the program coordination point for customer co-design and onboarding efforts.
Ensure customer expectations, constraints, and feedback are clearly communicated and tracked.
Support technical teams by managing structure, timelines, and communication.
Integration
Act as the program coordination point for integration activities, including alignment efforts and end-to-end tests.
Collect and synthesize requirements from integration partners and stakeholders, spanning functional and non-functional requirements (e.g. API payload vs API security).
Development
Align timelines, requirements and dependencies, with awareness of product, business and operational constraints.
Track progress and support documentation efforts.
Support reporting efforts for external stakeholders (e.g. NEDO program management).
Contribute to QuEra’s readiness for scaling gate-based quantum computing beyond Gemini, including operational and organizational considerations.

To achieve a balanced success in 1-4 above, the role will take responsibility for managing machine time across activities, machine use agreements, and regulatory requirements (e.g. data privacy, network security, etc.).

Qualification & Profile

Required:

Engineering background (e.g., semiconductor, systems engineering, advanced computing infrastructure).
Experience in technical program management, system delivery, or execution of complex technical products.
Strong ability to coordinate across multiple teams and external stakeholders.
Comfort in customer-facing, execution-oriented roles.
Strong communication, documentation, and organizational skills.

Preferred:

Experience with on-premise deployments and security/network-constrained environments.
Exposure to quantum computing, HPC, or advanced computing platforms.
Experience working with government, national lab, or research customers.
Demonstrated ability to learn new technical domains quickly.

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of delivering large-scale programs on time and within budget, leveraging automation and AI-driven analytics to improve processes. Not just a job, but a career

Yokogawa, award winner for ‘Best Asset Monitoring Technology’ and ‘Best Digital Twin Technology’ at the HP Awards, is a leading provider of industrial automation, test and measurement, information systems and industrial services in several industries.

Our aim is to shape a better future for our planet through supporting the energy transition, (bio)technology, artificial intelligence, industrial cybersecurity, etc. We are committed to the United Nations sustainable development goals by utilizing our ability to measure and connect.

About The Team

Our 18,000 employees work in over 60 countries with one corporate mission, to "co-innovate tomorrow". We are looking for dynamic colleagues who share our passion for technology and care for our planet. In return, we offer you great career opportunities to grow yourself in a truly global culture where respect, value creation, collaboration, integrity, and gratitude are highly valued and exhibited in everything we do.

Yokogawa is on the move, transforming itself from Industrial Automation to Industrial Autonomy (IA2IA) provider with advanced technologies allowing devices, equipment, business and production systems or even entire plants to operate autonomously. We were the world’s first company to develop a distributed process control system for the monitoring and control of various types of plant facilities, and we continue to evolve to meet our customer demanding needs. To help its customers keep pace with rapid advances in technology and an ever-changing business environment, Yokogawa provides solutions and services that will enable a digital transformation (DX) in their businesses, and is preparing the way for a future in which industries will make the transition from IA2IA. Bring your whole self to work each day and realize your greatest potential by enabling our customers to achieve world-class operational excellence! Join the transformation!

Job Summary

The Senior Program/Project Manager – SAP S/4HANA Upgrade (North America) is responsible for leading the North American workstream of a global SAP ECC-to-SAP S/4HANA transformation, with a planned go-live in 2028.

While the overall program is led by the global IT organization, this role owns planning and execution for the North American region, including implementation activities, local add-ons and integrations, user acceptance testing (UAT), training programs, change management, communications, and stakeholder alignment across all North American businesses and functions.

The role is aimed at a highly experienced SAP program/project manager with a strong track record in large, complex, multi-year SAP implementations and upgrades, particularly SAP S/4HANA.

Duties/Results

Act as the primary North American program/project lead within the global SAP S/4HANA program governance structure.
Develop and maintain the regional project plan (scope, timelines, milestones, dependencies, resources, budget) aligned with global standards and methodologies (e.g., SAP Activate / PMO framework).

Lead all North American implementation activities across requirements, solution design, build, testing, data migration, cutover planning, and post-go-live hypercare.
Manage local add-on developments, interfaces, and integrations required to support regional business processes and legacy systems.
Coordinate and oversee User Acceptance Testing (UAT) across all impacted business units, including test planning, test case definition, execution, defect management, and sign-off.
Define target user groups and role-based training needs in collaboration with business process owners and functional leads.
Oversee development of training content (classroom, virtual, e-learning, job aids) and ensure timely, high-quality training delivery to end users and key stakeholders.
Serve as a visible change champion, ensuring consistent messaging and engagement from leadership across the region.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior stakeholders across all North American business units, functions, and sites.
Proactively identify, assess, and manage program and project risks, issues, and dependencies; drive mitigation and contingency plans and ensure clear ownership.
Ensure adherence to global program standards, architecture principles, security and compliance requirements, and internal controls.
Monitor quality of deliverables from all internal and external teams; ensure that testing and validation processes meet agreed criteria before moving to subsequent phases.
Lead the regional hypercare phase after go-live, coordinating incident resolution, enhancement requests, and user support.
Capture lessons learned and improvement opportunities from North America and feed them back into global continuous improvement initiatives.
Support the transition from project mode to “business-as-usual” operations in collaboration with global IT, Shared Services, and business process owners.

Specifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Business, Engineering, or related field (Master’s degree preferred)
10–15+ years of overall IT project/program management experience, with a significant portion in ERP/SAP initiatives
Minimum 3–5 full life-cycle SAP implementations, including at least one large SAP S/4HANA program or ECC-to-S/4HANA conversion in a global or multi-region context
Proven experience managing large, cross-functional teams (IT, business, external partners) in a matrixed, international environment

Strong understanding of core SAP processes (e.g., Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, Record-to-Report, Manufacturing/Logistics) and how they are impacted by S/4HANA
Professional certifications such as PMP, Prince2, or Scrum/Agile; SAP S/4HANA or SAP project management certifications are a plus.

new_jobs.title: Production Program Manager, Space
new_jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

Anduril’s Space Manufacturing team is seeking a Production Program Manager to join our team. The Space Manufacturing team is responsible for the assembly, integration and test of complete space vehicles across multiple concurrent product lines, and for the manufacturing engineering, test operations and tooling that make those builds repeatable at rate. Your expertise will help ensure that our products meet the highest standards of quality and reliability at Anduril.

As a Production Program Manager, you will be a program leader responsible for planning, directing, and measuring the seamless execution and integration of the production work stream across multiple functions, including manufacturing engineering, supply chain, Quality, test, and design engineering. You will lead initiatives in collaboration with Business Line and Manufacturing Engineering to define, deploy, and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) across these functions during New Product Introduction, Limited Rate and Full Rate Production phases. These KPIs will span schedule, cost, risk management, product maturation, and resource utilization, in accordance with Anduril’s Manufacturing Development Process (MDP). You'll also own the manufacturing and Assembly, Integration, and Test (AIT) execution plan — schedule, risk, KPIs and gate readiness. It does not own the engineering work itself; manufacturing engineering, test operations and quality are owned by their respective leads.

What You’ll Do

Partner with planning, production, manufacturing engineering, design engineering, supply chain, quality, launch operations and business line leadership on strategic priorities and delivery commitments.
Own the integrated manufacturing and AIT schedule across multiple product lines: build it, maintain it as the schedule of record, and run the critical path and execution-risk analysis leadership decides from.
Drive execution against that schedule week to week: convene the cross-functional cadence, hold owners to dates, surface slips early with quantified impact, and drive recovery plans rather than reporting variance after the fact.
Define, deploy and monitor manufacturing KPIs from New Product Introduction through full rate production per Anduril's Manufacturing Development Process, and build the gate-readiness and critical-path reporting leadership acts on.
Build and maintain the production cost model with Sourcing, Manufacturing Engineering and Finance. This model is the principal basis for strategic decisions on production design, operations and resource allocation.
Serve as the manufacturing and AIT counterpart to the program managers and chief engineers, carrying delegated authority from the Director of Manufacturing to conduct manufacturing and AIT gates.
Own manufacturing and AIT risk: maintain the risk register, quantify schedule and cost exposure, drive mitigation to closure, and make the trade between accepting risk and holding a gate explicit rather than implicit.
Integrate the manufacturing engineering, test operations and MEP process steps into the program plan and capture that scope correctly within NRE so the work is funded rather than absorbed.
Represent production up and out: contribute proposal and Basis of Estimate content for manufacturing and AIT scope, present at milestone reviews, and brief customers and business line leadership on execution status, gate readiness and risk.
Engage principal vendors and partners alongside Sourcing to hold delivery commitments and contract compliance and integrate their milestones into the schedule as dependencies with real dates.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering or a related technical discipline.
8+ years in program, project or production management in aerospace, space, defense or another complex hardware industry.
3+ years owning schedule and execution for a hardware program.
Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.
Has personally owned an integrated master schedule as the schedule of record — built the network, maintained it, ran critical path — with network-level fluency in Microsoft Project, Primavera P6 or Smartsheet: logic, float, resource loading and baselines.
Experience managing a program through a New Product Introduction transition into rate production, with the readiness gates and reviews that go with it (PDR, CDR, MRR, TRR, PRR or equivalents).
Has held a date or a gate against pressure from a peer organization and can describe how it was resolved. This role fails without it.
Demonstrated risk and performance management on a hardware program: a maintained risk register with quantified exposure and mitigations driven to closure, plus KPIs that changed a decision where you can explain the mechanism.
Has represented a production or program organization up and out: contributed proposal and Basis of Estimate content, and briefed customers or executive leadership on status, readiness and risk. Both the written and the in-person sides matter here.
Has built or owned a production cost model — unit cost, labor content, material cost, NRE versus recurring — and used it to drive a decision on capacity, make/buy or resource allocation.
Spacecraft or satellite program experience, including integration and test campaign scheduling and environmental test sequencing.
Took a hardware program from single-digit annual builds into rate production of 100+ units per year.
Earned value management or control account ownership, and experience capturing manufacturing scope correctly within NRE.
Managed supplier and partner delivery commitments alongside Sourcing, including contract compliance and recovery on a late supplier.
PMP, Agile, Lean or Six Sigma credentials, and working fluency in Jira, Confluence and Smartsheet.

US Salary Range

$146,000—$194,000 USD

Benefits

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind

No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

The Third-Party Security Manager is responsible for leading and maturing the organization's Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program. The position works closely with Information Security, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, Privacy, Enterprise Risk Management, and business stakeholders to ensure third-party relationships align with organizational risk tolerance, regulatory requirements, and security standards. Compensation

Compensation at Guild is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to local and federal minimum wage requirements, education, level of experience, and applicant’s geographical location.

Essential Functions

Develop, maintain, and continuously improve the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) framework, policies, standards, and procedures.
Establish risk-based processes for onboarding, reviewing, monitoring, and offboarding third parties.
Define vendor risk assessment methodologies and risk scoring criteria.
Ensure alignment with regulatory requirements and industry frameworks including NIST, SOC 2, ISO 27001, FFIEC, GLBA, PCI-DSS, and applicable privacy regulations.
Conduct security, privacy, operational, compliance, and business continuity risk assessments for new and existing vendors.
Review vendor security documentation including: SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports, ISO certifications, Penetration test reports, Vulnerability management reports, Security questionnaires, Business continuity and disaster recovery plans,
Identify control gaps and work with vendors and stakeholders on remediation plans.

Facilitate periodic vendor reviews and risk re-assessments.

The Program Manager (PM) serves as the senior leader responsible for overall execution, compliance, and performance of the UC‑12 CLS program supporting the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps’ global fleet of UC‑12F/M/W aircraft. The PM is the primary interface with the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO), Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), Utility Lift IPT, and government site Technical Points of Contact (TPOCs), ensuring transparent communication, timely reporting, and continuous performance improvement.

As the PM, you will manage the effort for operating and maintaining the fleet of aircraft, aircraft subsystems, and support equipment. The Program Manager will develop and maintain systems to oversee all aircraft maintenance and personnel, materials and inspections, launch and recovery of the aircraft, supply of all Contractor owned spares and support equipment through a Contractor Owned and Maintained Parts (COMP); repair and overhaul of all repairable spares at Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certified repair stations; maintenance and repair of all support equipment; aircraft paint; engine repair and overhaul.

Lead Overall Program Execution

Serve as Primary Government Interface

Manage Personnel & Key Staff

Ensure all required positions are staffed, certified, and compliant with FAA, Navy, and PWS requirements. Oversee site leads and A&P-certified mechanics.

Oversee Performance Metrics

Monitor and ensure aircraft Mission Capable rates, maintenance turnaround times, and logistics responsiveness meet contract performance standards.

Direct Quality & Airworthiness Compliance

Maintain a compliant Quality Assurance Program, ensure proper maintenance documentation, and enforce FAA/NAVAIR standards for airworthiness.

Manage Logistics & Property

Oversee aircraft parts, support equipment, inventory accuracy, freight forwarding, hazardous material handling, and GFP accountability.

Coordinate Depot-Level & Engineering Activities

Support depot repairs, ACIs, engine/propeller overhauls, technical directives, and engineering investigations or modifications.

Ensure Accurate Reporting & Data Management

Deliver all required CDRLs, maintain WIS accuracy, and submit mission capability, aircraft status, safety, funds status, and configuration reports.

Lead Transition-In & Transition-Out

Manage personnel onboarding, inventories, audits, and turnover activities during contract start-up and close-out.

Manage Risk & Program Improvements

Identify risks early, implement mitigation plans, and drive continuous improvement across maintenance, logistics, and operational processes.

Assisting in the growth of Amentum's revenue in Navy/Marine Corps Aviation sector.

Overview

Project Manager-Information Services Senior

Our leaders shape strategic initiatives, develop enthusiastic teams, and work to improve health outcomes. They advance our mission and exemplify excellence, compassion, teamwork, and purpose in all that they do .
Indiana University Health is seeking individuals who embody these values to join our Information Services team in the role of Project Manager-Information Services Senior.

Summary

The Field Project Manager (FPM) serves as the Information Services (IS) representative within the construction environment for Strategic Projects. This role builds and maintains strong partnerships with Design & Construction (D&C), low voltage vendors, trade partners, and the Strategic Project Manager (SPM) to ensure IS requirements are executed accurately and on schedule.

While the SPM focuses broadly across IS, Operations, and Clinical domains, the FPM is dedicated to ensuring the construction team implements IS design intent, standards, and installation quality in real time. The FPM acts as an on-site resource, liaison, and validator throughout the construction lifecycle.

Leads and directs high-priority and complex project(s) usually encompassing multiple applications and business areas to successful and timely completion and within budget. This role involves coordinating with multiple teams and governance groups. Provides administrative decision making, leadership and planning for IU Health's business and clinical projects. Assures day-to-day coordination, communications, issue/resolution, and financial management related to the assigned projects. Oversees resources assigned to the project must be familiar with the systems scope and project objectives, as well as the role and function of each team member to effectively coordinate the activities of the team. Facilitates current and future state business processes, requirements, elicitation, solutions and development and test management.

Candidate Qualifications

Candidates for the position will be evaluated according to the following criteria and competencies.

Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent experience.
5-7 years of relevant experience.
PMP (Project Management Process) certification is required or requirement to attain within 12 months.
Required experience with enterprise PPM (Project and Portfolio Management) tools.
Strong working skills with MS Office tools such as MS Project, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Vizio etc. is required.
Required experience with contractor and vendor management.
Requires a demonstrated fundamental understanding of project accounting and financial management.

Leadership -

Communication -
Shares thoughts and information in a clear, concise, and professional manner, in both oral and written communication formats. Demonstrates active listening and seeks further information to ensure clarity and understanding. Promptly responds to requests for information and works to proactively think through next steps and anticipate potential issues, requests, or business needs. Openly shares knowledge and expertise.

Ethical Practice -
Maintains confidentiality as appropriate, earns trust and respect of others, and exhibits behaviors that express the ethical practice of a healthcare organization. Mitigates unintended consequences through careful analysis and observation of business practices.

Critical Thinking -
Leverages curiosity and insights to explore rationale behind decision-making. Connect pieces of information from various sources to improve problem solving capabilities and recommendations. Actively distinguishes questions, problems, and conflict. Combines existing knowledge and on-the-job experiences to ensure best practices are being implemented in day-to-day work.

Addresses problems directly and implements objectives effectively. Produces on time high-quality work deliverables. Able to apply basic project management principles and ensure standard of work is place and reflects leading best practices. Applied earned value principles to managing projects, resource planning and estimates at completion.

Customer Focus -
Identifies short- and long-term customer needs and ensures the effective delivery of high quality and value-added solutions, products, and services that meet or exceed customer expectations.

Develops solutions with sound methodologies, guidelines, and best practices; makes decisions and solve problems within project plan parameters. Identifies patterns and potential underlying issues. Choosing best alternative based on consideration of pros, cons, and weighing various tradeoffs.

You are an exceptional relationship builder, translator, and team advocate. Rather than focusing on hands-on technical execution, your strength lies in your ability to navigate organizational dynamics, influence stakeholders across diverse teams, and translate complex data points into compelling narratives that drive business outcomes.

Lead, mentor, and protect a lean team of technical analysts, providing the necessary "air cover" for them to focus on deep execution while actively coaching them on communication and influencing skills.

Strong experience within the technology industry
Extensive knowledge of product operations, business insights, program management, or a related role—ideally within a fast-paced SaaS, product, or engineering organization.
A strong background of direct people management experience, with a proven track record of hiring, developing, and leading high-performing teams.
Exceptional communication, executive presence, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and build consensus among senior leadership.
Proven track record of working closely with cross-functional stakeholders (Product, Engineering, Customer Success, Finance) and successfully influencing decision-making without direct authority.
Strong storytelling and presentation skills, with a demonstrated ability to turn complex technical data into simple, actionable insights for senior leadership.
Ability to manage a high volume of incoming requests, establish clear operational triage frameworks, and comfortably manage stakeholder expectations.
A solid understanding of how product analytics and reporting structures operate (e.g., data flows, modeling, or visualization tools) to effectively translate technical needs, though hands-on coding/modeling is not required.
Deep understanding of modern development methodologies (e.g., Agile, SAFe) and the product lifecycle in a SaaS context.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility.

Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt.

We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard — from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

The Role

The Project Manager – Specialty Program Manager, Global Artisan Innovation Center will serve as the central program leader and primary point of contact between General Motors Defense (GMD), other Specialty Programs and the Global Artisan Innovation Center/PPO organization. This role will establish and lead a structured work-intake, evaluation, and approval process for new Business and ultra-low volume opportunities, ensuring that requests are assessed consistently for capacity, staffing, cost, tooling, process impacts, capital requirements, and schedule feasibility before commitments are made.

The position will coordinate cross-functional teams, lead feasibility and cost-estimating activities, manage strategic studies, and develop repeatable processes that support sustainable GM growth opportunities while protecting existing GAIC/PPO core work commitments.

What You'll Do

Serve as the primary interface between GMD & other specialty customers and GAIC/PPO for new work requests, studies, and business opportunities.
Establish and maintain a single, disciplined intake funnel for all non-traditional requests.
Lead cross-functional review forums involving Manufacturing Engineering, Body, General Assembly, MTS, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Facilities, Strategy and Planning and other stakeholders, including regular interaction and providing direction to Program Teams to influence design and buildability for overall program success.
Develop agendas, decision criteria, governance practices, and approval recommendations for opportunity reviews.
Direct assessments of:
Organizational and production capacity, working with the scheduling team in Program Management.
Salaried and hourly manpower requirements
Staffing availability and workforce risks
Tooling, equipment, and process impacts
Capital investment requirements
Cost estimates, Manufacturing Planning Studies (MPS) and business-case assumptions
Schedule feasibility, timing, and execution risk

Coordinate detailed program studies from initial request through recommendation and leadership decision and discussion.
Lead studies as a pilot for the future opportunities-evaluation model as we develop standardized work processes.
Ensure vehicle content, MTS, Body, General Assembly, scope are clearly understood before commitments are made. Driving to a total-enterprise solution that delivers on SPQRC&E metrics.
Establish consistent communication routines and status reporting between GAIC/PPO and Program stakeholders.
Prevent unauthorized commitments by ensuring requests are evaluated through the approved process.
Develop repeatable standards, templates, tools, and lessons learned for future studies.
Identify risks, constraints, dependencies, and escalation needs; develop mitigation plans with functional leaders.
Partner with shop leadership to evaluate staffing projections, retirements, workforce reductions, apprentice development, and advance-hiring needs.
Support strategic capacity planning and resource prioritization across competing GAIC/PPO and GMD requirements.
Provide Sr. Leader and Executive-level updates, recommendations, and decision packages to leadership.
Influence stakeholders across organizational boundaries without direct authority.
Promote disciplined program-management practices, accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement

Core Competencies

Manufacturing program interaction
Strategic planning and prioritization
Cross-functional collaboration
Capacity and workforce planning
Cost and feasibility analysis
Risk and issue management
Stakeholder alignment and communication
Executive influence
Process development and standardization
Decision-making and accountability
Continuous improvement
Operational and manufacturing acumen

Measures of Success

All requests are routed through a defined and consistently applied intake process.
Opportunity decisions are supported by documented capacity, staffing, cost, tooling, capital, and schedule assessments.
GAIC/PPO & program team stakeholders receive clear, timely, and consistent communication.
Study Opportunities establishes a repeatable standardized model for evaluating future opportunities.
Program risks, assumptions, and resource constraints are identified early and escalated appropriately to all stakeholders.
GAIC/PPO growth is aligned with sustainable capacity and workforce plans.
Cross-functional leaders have confidence in the quality, transparency, and timeliness of recommendations.

Working Relationships

This position will work closely with:

GMD program and business-development teams
GAIC/PPO leadership and shop management
Manufacturing, Body, General Assembly, MTS, engineering, quality, and finance
Tooling, facilities, capital planning, and workforce-planning teams
Program Teams and their stakeholders
Space and facilities governance teams
Executive and senior leadership

Leadership Expectations

The successful candidate will demonstrate enterprise-level ownership, maintain a disciplined and impartial evaluation process, and build trust across Specialty Program Teams and GAIC/PPO. They will balance growth opportunities with current commitments, protect organizational capacity, and ensure that leadership decisions are based on complete, transparent, and fact-based information.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, project management, or a related field or equivalent launch experience.
Significant experience leading complex, cross-functional programs in manufacturing, engineering, product development, defense, or a related environment.
Demonstrated experience with program planning, resource and capacity analysis, cost estimating, risk management, and executive communication.
Experience coordinating multiple functional organizations and managing competing priorities.
Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, tooling, equipment, facilities, General Assembly, and production-readiness considerations.
Proven ability to establish structure and governance in an ambiguous or developing work environment.
Strong written, verbal, facilitation, negotiation, and presentation skills.
Ability to make sound recommendations using incomplete information and clearly communicate assumptions, risks, and tradeoffs.
Proficiency with standard project-management, financial-analysis, and collaboration tools.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

Master’s degree or advanced certification in project or program management.
Experience supporting Vehicle Launch as an aMIM or Plant Launch role.
Experience with Manufacturing Planning Studies (MPS’s).
Familiar with General Motors Defense or other defense-related programs.
Familiarity with the Global Vehicle Development Plan (GVDP).
Experience with vehicle manufacturing, machining, body operations, General Assembly, or prototype and low-volume production.
Experience developing work-intake, portfolio-governance, or business-case processes.
Interaction & coordination with Strategy and Planning teams.
Knowledge of GM manufacturing systems, governance practices, and cross-functional decision processes.
Experience with workforce planning, apprentice pipelines, succession planning, or capacity modeling.

This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc). new_jobs.description:
# DATA ANALYST – FRAUD INTELLIGENCE

## About the Role

Sardine is seeking a Data Analyst to join its Fraud Intelligence team at the intersection of data evaluation, vendor strategy, and fraud detection. You’ll serve as the analytical engine behind evaluating, testing, and onboarding third-party data signals and vendor partnerships, determining which data assets improve fraud outcomes for clients.

This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role working closely with the Head of Fraud, Product, Data Engineering, and client-facing teams. You’ll build rigorous evaluation frameworks, analyze vendor data, quantify fraud-signal value, and translate complex findings into actionable recommendations for a fast-moving, data-driven environment.

## Key Responsibilities

- Design and execute structured evaluation frameworks to assess the quality, coverage, and fraud-signal value of incoming vendor data assets.
- Build lift analyses, backtests, and champion/challenger comparisons to quantify the incremental value of new data signals against the existing fraud detection stack.
- Profile vendor datasets for completeness, freshness, match rates, and population coverage across industries such as crypto, fintech, neobanks, and e-commerce.
- Collaborate with fraud leadership to define evaluation criteria tied to real-world fraud outcomes.
- Analyze false positive rates, catch rates, and precision/recall tradeoffs when evaluating fraud signals.
- Translate vendor data findings into clear recommendations, including whether to adopt, pilot, deprioritize, or decline a data asset.
- Partner with Data Engineering to define data ingestion requirements and ensure testing environments reflect production-like conditions.
- Document evaluation results and maintain an internal knowledge base of vendor data performance over time.
- Conduct ad hoc deep dives into fraud trends, model performance, and client-specific data questions.
- Work with cross-functional stakeholders to translate complex analytical findings into actionable fraud intelligence.

## Required Qualifications

- 3–5 years of experience in data analysis, data science, or a related analytical role.
- Proficiency in SQL.
- Proficiency in Python or R for data manipulation, statistical analysis, and visualization.
- Solid understanding of evaluation metrics and statistical concepts, including:
- Precision and recall
- AUC/ROC
- Lift
- Population distributions
- A/B testing fundamentals
- Experience working with external or third-party datasets, including evaluating data quality, match rates, and signal value.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

new_jobs.title: IT Security Analyst
new_jobs.description:
About the Company

Corporate Imaging Concepts (CIC) is a branded merchandise and e-commerce company headquartered in Northbrook, Illinois, with a full warehouse and operations facility in Alpharetta, Georgia. CIC builds and runs online storefronts and fulfillment programs for enterprise clients, which means the company manages payment flows, customer data, and the security expectations that come with serving large organizations.

About the Role

The IT Security Analyst owns security as a discipline for CIC, including security posture, compliance, vendor risk, and incident response. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with broad ownership and visible impact. The role partners closely with the Infrastructure Manager, who owns networks, servers, and endpoints as systems, while this position owns the security controls, policies, and compliance obligations that sit on top of them and the role would be reporting directly to IT leadership. CIC has a small IT team, so this role requires comfort with shared team responsibilities. Security is the primary mandate, but the IT Security Analyst should also expect to support ticket management and hands-on infrastructure support alongside the Infrastructure Manager. The right candidate values variety, pragmatism, and the opportunity to secure the full environment of a growing company without overbuilding an enterprise-scale security program.

Responsibilities

Security Posture & Controls

Own day-to-day security posture, including identity and access controls such as MFA, conditional access, and privileged accounts.
Support endpoint protection, email security, and patching priorities in partnership with Infrastructure.
Monitor and triage alerts using appropriately scaled tooling and recommend where tooling should or should not grow.
Advise leadership on security risk in clear, prioritized terms, including what matters now, what can wait, and what it costs.

Compliance, Documentation & Vendor Risk

Own client-facing security compliance, including security questionnaires and vendor risk assessments.
Maintain security documentation and policies that are practical, current, and appropriate for CIC’s size and environment.
Support payment cards, PCI-related obligations with CIC’s processing partners.
Run vendor security reviews for the platforms and integrations CIC relies on.

Incident Response & Awareness

Own the incident response process, including first-line triage, coordination during events, and post-incident follow-through.
Run right-sized security awareness activities, including phishing simulation, onboarding training, and practical guidance people can follow.

Shared IT Team Responsibilities

Work on the support queue by triaging, resolving, and managing user support tickets as part of the IT team’s shared rotation.
Provide hands-on infrastructure support alongside the Infrastructure Manager, including endpoints, accounts, Microsoft 365 administration, and day-to-day systems work as needed.

Qualifications

3-6 years of hands-on security experience in an analyst or engineer role, with recent personal experience deploying, tuning, and maintaining security controls.
Practical depth in Microsoft 365 / Entra ID security, endpoint protection, and email security.
Experience answering client security questionnaires or completing vendor risk assessments, including the ability to triage large, detailed assessments against deadlines.
Working familiarity with PCI-DSS concepts; experience in an e-commerce, retail, or SaaS environment is a strong plus.
Strong judgment to operate as a one-person security function, including prioritizing strategically, deferring accurately, and communicating clearly.
Genuine comfort with generalist IT work, including support tickets and infrastructure tasks.
Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, or SSCP is welcome; senior certifications are not required.

Preferred Skills

MSP or small-team IT background with experience managing breadth, ticket discipline, and shifting priorities.
SOC 2 or similar attestation exposure, either client-side or audit-side.
Experience with Azure security tooling and scripting such as PowerShell or Python for automation.
Experience working alongside SAP or other ERP environments.

What This Role Is Not

This is not a management role with direct reports, a pure-security seat, or a SOC shift position. Part of the week will include support tickets and infrastructure work because CIC operates with a small IT team. The opportunity is to serve as the security function for a growing company with real ownership from day one and room for the role to grow as the business grows.

Why This Role Matters

The IT Security Analyst helps protect CIC’s people, clients, data, systems, and brand reputation. This role brings practical structure to security and compliance while staying grounded in the realities of a hands-on, fast-moving business.

Location and pay

Hybrid from our Northbrook, IL headquarters or our Alpharetta, GA warehouse and operations facility — regular onsite presence is part of the role, given the hands-on infrastructure and support responsibilities at both sites. Candidates should be within commuting distance of Northbrook or Alpharetta. Base salary range $95,000–$110,000 depending on experience, plus benefits.

This position blends cybersecurity consulting and risk management with system, infrastructure, and security engineering support to help business and IT teams reduce risk and improve control maturity.

The IPS Consulting Security Analyst must have a combination of written and verbal communication skills, interpersonal skills, the ability to influence, guide, and/or lead others necessary to accomplish IPS goals, and the technical capability to assist IT teams with the implementation, configuration, and tuning of security controls.

new_jobs.title: IT & Security Manager
new_jobs.description:
The role

As Wayve grows across continents, we are looking for a Corporate Security Engineering Manager to own the systems and controls layer the whole company runs on: identity, endpoint, device and asset lifecycle, SaaS, and the and the security controls implemented in all of them. Most of this role is platform ownership. You will lead a distributed team of engineers across the UK, Germany and the US.

This is a build role. We are standing this layer up properly for the first time, so you will shape how it works rather than inherit someone else's design, and the team and headcount to do it are already approved.

It is one of three peer leadership roles in our infrastructure, IT and security function, all reporting to the same Head of IT. One peer owns the network estate, one owns our global support service, and you own the platforms and the controls. You will also work closely with our central Security team and with the engineering teams whose work depends the platforms you own.

You will do well here if you like owning platforms end to end, turning manual work into automation, and growing the engineers around you.

Key responsibilities

Own the operation of our corporate security controls: endpoint hardening, identity and access, privileged access, vulnerability and patch management, and access reviews.
Partner with our central Security team on policy, vulnerability management and incident response. They own those processes; you make them real in the IT environment.
Own Okta and everything on it: application onboarding, SSO and SAML migration, group and attribute automation, the application catalogue, and the automation that grants and revokes access. Our Helpdesk Lead runs the joiner, mover and leaver process itself; you own the platform it runs on and the evidence that access was revoked.
Own endpoint management across a genuinely mixed Mac, Windows and Linux fleet, covering enrolment, baselines, patching and compliance reporting.
Own device and asset lifecycle and SaaS and licensing, including records, reconciliation, audit process, inventory accuracy, tenant administration and vendor relationships.
Lead, grow and hire a distributed team across three countries and several time zones, and develop engineers into domain owners with clear standards behind each domain.
Partner with the Helpdesk Lead on what gets automated away, with the Network Manager on work that crosses both lines such as 802.1x and device posture, and act as the function's interface to compliance on identity, endpoint and asset controls.
Turn certification requirements into implemented controls, and into evidence the platform produces on demand.

About you

In order to set you up for success as a Corporate Security Engineering Manager at Wayve, we are looking for the following skills and experience.

Essential

Experience leading an IT, security or infrastructure team, including hiring, performance management and developing engineers.
Deep hands-on background in corporate IT platforms: identity (Okta or Entra), endpoint management at fleet scale (Iru, Jamf, Intune or equivalent), and SaaS administration.
Hands-on Linux fleet management alongside Mac and Windows.
Practical security operations experience: endpoint hardening, vulnerability and patch management, incident response, access reviews, and privileged access or zero-trust access delivery.
Delivered against a security certification or audit (TISAX, ISO 27001, SOC 2 or equivalent) on the implementation and evidence side.
Scripting or infrastructure-as-code ability, enough to set the standard and review your team's work.
Experience scaling a corporate estate through fast growth and multi-site expansion.
Holds a clear boundary with peer managers, and is honest about risk upward as well as downward.

Desirable

Experience of a supplier-security assessment in an automotive or OEM supply chain.
Has stood up a corporate security capability from scratch rather than inheriting a mature one.
Hands-on with 802.1x and certificate-based device posture from the identity and endpoint side.
Exposure to offices, labs, garages and test facilities rather than offices alone, or to AI development environments.

This is a full-time role based in our office in London. At Wayve we want the best of all worlds so we operate a hybrid working policy that combines time together in our offices and workshops to fuel innovation, culture, relationships and learning, and time spent working from home.

to support Numerix SaaS clients by monitoring market data generation processes used by Numerix Financial Systems to ensure the integrity and the quality of market data as part of Numerix Data Management (NXDM) framework. This role involves technical and functional support, incident management, and coordination with clients and internal teams (P&E, PS, etc.), contributing directly to operational excellence and client satisfaction.

What You'll Do:

Define, implement, and execute standard operating procedures for Numerix clients’ market data operation processes.
Perform daily monitoring and verification of market data deliveries—including scheduled intraday and end-of-day snapshots for multiple clients—by checking the success or failure of runs, batch processes, and data feeds to ensure operational integrity and SLA compliance.
Enhance existing processes through optimization and automation of manual checks.
Respond to daily requests for operational support activities related to market data queries, raised by both our clients and internal groups.
Monitor, triage, and resolve technical and data quality issues related to Numerix data feeds, escalating to developers, vendors, or other stakeholders as needed.
Engage with vendors to address inquiries related to market data availability, delivery or quality.
Coordinate NXDM releases and production patch deployments with clients, and support development teams in executing and validating parallel runs.
Act as Incident Manager in accordance with incident management policies for market data incidents, leading Post-Mortem review and root cause analysis to drive continuous improvement.
Assist Numerix clients (financial institutions) with our API platform for market data related issues and queries.

What We're Looking For:

Bachelor’s degree from a leading engineering university, or equivalent professional experience.
Good experience in Python for ad-hoc data analysis and automating manual processes.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; practical exposure to SQL is beneficial for the role.
Understanding of exchange-traded and OTC derivatives (e.g., forwards, futures, options) across multiple asset classes, including IR, commodities, credit, equities, and FX. Familiarity with financial concepts such as volatility and beta is advantageous.
Working Knowledge of Cloud Services, ideally AWS (Step Functions, Lambda, EC2, DynamoDB, etc.) is a plus.
Strong troubleshooting abilities and good English communication skills.
Willingness to work in US shift when required (3:00 PM to 11:30 PM MST).

Extra Credit:

Understanding of multiple asset classes (IR, Commodities, Credit, Equities, FX).
Ability to use Excel, Python and SQL for ad-hoc data analysis and investigation of market data issues.

Where You’ll Work:

This is a fully remote role open to anyone who is authorized to work in India.

An important note on salary:

The annual pay range for this position is based on the preferred primary location of the role which is listed above. If you are applying to this role at a location that is not the preferred primary location, please keep in mind the salary range will vary and may fall outside of what is listed. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

new_jobs.title: Revenue Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

The Revenue Operations Analyst will join Epsilon’s Revenue Operations team in a foundational support role designed to strengthen day-to-day operational support for sales leaders and business partners. This role will help own operational and execution-oriented responsibilities related to revenue operations, creating clearer focus across the team and enabling business unit partners and functional RevOps leads to stay aligned to their core areas of ownership across business partnership, process design, governance, analytics, and systems implementation.

This is a strong opportunity for someone who is detail-oriented, organized, comfortable working with data, and interested in building depth in how revenue operations supports sales execution across a complex business. The role will provide hands-on exposure to CRM data quality, sales process and systems administration, reporting support, intake tracking, documentation, and cross-functional coordination.

Responsibilities

Sales Leader and Business Partner Support

Provide operational and coordination support to sales leaders and RevOps business unit partners across recurring sales operations activities.
Help track, organize, and follow up on sales support requests, intake items, and open operational tasks.
Prepare and maintain recurring materials, trackers, summaries, and status updates used by sales leadership and RevOps stakeholders.

CRM, Data Quality, and Process Administration

Assist with CRM data hygiene activities, including identifying missing, outdated, inconsistent, or duplicate information.
Support maintenance of account, opportunity, pipeline, forecast, and sales activity data according to established RevOps standards.
Help ensure sales teams are following defined processes, required fields, naming conventions, and data entry expectations.

Reporting and Analytics Support

Support recurring sales and pipeline reporting by gathering inputs, validating data, refreshing standard reports, and preparing summaries for review.
Assist with basic analysis of sales operations data, including pipeline movement, activity tracking, data completeness, and process adherence.
Partner with Revenue Intelligence and business partners to clarify reporting requests and ensure needed inputs are captured accurately.
Help document reporting definitions, field usage, and business rules to support consistency across revenue reporting.

Documentation, Enablement, and Continuous Improvement

Create and maintain documentation for repeatable sales operations processes, support workflows, and RevOps operating procedures.
Support training and enablement efforts by helping prepare job aids, process guides, checklists, and simple how-to materials.

What Success Looks Like

Sales leaders and business partners receive timely, accurate support on recurring operational needs.
Operational work is organized, tracked, and completed consistently.
CRM and sales operations data is complete, accurate, and aligned to established standards.
Recurring reports, trackers, and process documentation are maintained with strong attention to detail.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in revenue operations, sales operations, analytics, marketing, or a related field.
Strong attention to detail and ability to manage recurring tasks accurately and consistently.
Comfort working with data, spreadsheets, trackers, and structured processes.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; ability to learn CRM and reporting tools quickly.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to summarize information clearly.
Highly organized, proactive, and able to manage multiple requests in a fast-paced environment.
Interest in revenue operations, sales operations, business process improvement, or go-to-market operations.

Preferred

Relevant experience through internships, coursework, project work, or prior roles in sales operations, revenue operations, business operations, analytics, finance, or marketing operations.
Exposure to Salesforce or another CRM platform.
Experience building or maintaining trackers, reports, dashboards, process documentation, or project status updates.
Familiarity with sales pipeline, forecasting, account management, lead/opportunity workflows, or commercial operations concepts.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is someone who is eager to learn, takes pride in accuracy, and is motivated by improving process, organization, and operational consistency. They are comfortable with operational detail, able to follow and improve repeatable processes, and interested in growing within revenue operations over time. This person should be service-oriented, dependable, and willing to lean into the details that help sales leaders and business partners work more effectively.

This role can serve as a foundation for growth into the Revenue Operations function. As the analyst builds experience, they may take on more advanced ownership of reporting, process improvement, CRM administration, project coordination, or business unit partnership support.

new_jobs.title: Business Analyst II FPB
new_jobs.description:
At First PREMIER Bank and PREMIER Bankcard, we’ve created a culture that emphasizes personal success, respect, health, and wellness, fun and giving back. This is an environment where you will be rewarded, valued, and celebrated for your hard work.

We offer a robust and expanded package of health benefits, incentives, paid time off and growth and career advancement opportunities. We celebrate our employees and show our appreciation with private concerts, outdoor bashes, cash and car giveaways and more! See some of our epic celebrations and employee recognitions.

Considered one of the nation’s strongest financial organizations, we’ve achieved our success by embodying the views and values of The PREMIER Way. From our CEOs to the newest hires, we all follow these shared views and values to guide us on how to treat our customers, co-workers and communities. The PREMIER Way also serves as a roadmap on how to be successful inside and outside of the workplace. We believe in investing in our employees, their families and our communities.

Job Description

Location:
Sioux Falls, SD

Shift:
Monday - Friday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM

Company:
First PREMIER Bank

About The Role

Supports day-to-day business operations by managing report requests, maintaining data accuracy, and ensuring reliable information delivery across assigned business units. This role emphasizes hands-on data analysis, troubleshooting, and basic to moderate report generation, with a focus on execution and strategic design.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Essential duties and responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

Provides data-driven insights to bank-level managers, including retail, loan servicing, and credit teams. Responds to data requests by reviewing existing reports, offering alternative solutions when the exact data is unavailable, ensuring that all stakeholders receive relevant and actionable information.
Masters and maintains expertise in internal software and report writing systems by proactively learning updates, utilizing vendor resources, and staying informed on changes that impact business analytics. Demonstrates self-sufficiency in understanding and applying new features to improve report and analytic processes.
Develops a strong understanding of the systems generating data by exploring data sources and learning system structures. Uses this knowledge to ask the right questions to clarify business needs, and translates them into comprehensive, accurate reports. Regularly creates data extracts for various interfaces.
Builds strong relationships with management teams to become the primary point of contact for report requests, assessing availability and feasibility. Develops guides for managers on how to pull reports, serving as the subject matter expert for department leads. Collaborates with other areas to review and update procedures, ensuring accuracy and consistency across the organization.

new_jobs.description:
Company: CGIC

Department: Claims

Employment Type: Regular Full-Time

Work Model: Hybrid (2 days in office)

Language: Bilingualism in English and French is an asset.

The Opportunity

We are a leading Canadian financial services co-operative committed to being a catalyst for a sustainable and resilient society and our team is essential to deliver on this strategy. That’s why we prioritize our people, to ensure we provide a strong culture and development opportunities which enables our team to thrive and to live our purpose. The best part is that you will work with people that care passionately about you, our clients and our communities.

Our Claims team aspires to create peace of mind for our clients and our communities. Our national team of knowledgeable and trusted professionals serve our clients with compassion. We are passionate about continuous improvement and operate with high-integrity, motivated by our desire to do the right thing for our clients.

As Data Analyst, you actively contribute to various initiatives by analyzing data to solve business problems and providing valuable insights. You understand the insurance business domain and ensure your own tasks contribute to meeting the business objectives by applying appropriate methods and critical thinking and performing analysis.

How You Will Create Impact

Autonomously perform descriptive and diagnostic analysis using recommended methods (ex: regression, cohort analysis, cluster analysis, A/B testing, factor analysis).
Design and develop metrics to enable descriptive analysis and diagnostic analysis.
Autonomously design proof of concept and deliver with guidance a prototype analytical solution to enable effective storytelling and descriptive/diagnostic analysis.
Work on Data querying (T-SQL, SQL, MySQL, etc.)
Extract, clean, reconcile and prepare the data required for the analysis.
Autonomously communicate findings to colleagues and your manager in an effective manner.

To Join Our Team

You have 3-5 years of relevant experience in Business Intelligence or other relevant domain.
You have a University Degree in Business Intelligence, Computer Science, Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or equivalent technical experience.
ACAS or FCAS designations are considered an asset.
You have experience solving standard problems by analyzing possible solutions by using our experience, judgment and precedent & challenging status quo.
You have good knowledge and understanding of data analysis, programing, modeling techniques, data warehouse and data management, research, architecture and design.
Experience with the following technologies is required: Sql, Python, R, Microsoft Fabric
Experience with the following technologies is an asset: Service now , Jira, Databricks

How You Will Succeed

You influence change and are committed to continuous improvement, in order to exceed client expectations.
You leverage critical thinking skills to identify problems and proactively propose solutions.
Your strong communication skills allow you to clearly convey messages.
You’re an effective team player who shares knowledge to support our peers.

What You Need To Know

You will be subject to a Background check as a condition of employment, in the event you are the successful candidate.

What’s in it for you?

Training and development opportunities to grow your career.
Flexible work options and paid time off to support your personal and family needs.
A holistic approach to your well-being, with physical and mental health programs and a supportive workplace culture.
Paid volunteer days to give back to your community.
In addition to our competitive salary and incentive programs, eligible employees also benefit from a comprehensive total rewards package including group retirement savings plans, pension and benefits (e.g., health and wellness, dental, disability and life coverage), mental health support and an employee assistance program.
